text: Build job 5, part 1, of the records-history plan (docs/design/records-history.md sections 5.2, 6 and 10, decision D111): an attribution check that reads only athena/records, never commit-message trailers. It walks main's first-parent commits from the commit the first landing-intent record expects as its base onward, and requires each to be named as host_commit by a landing record whose head tree equals that commit's tree and whose expected base is its parent; a commit with a matching landing-intent but no landing record yet is pending for 15 minutes from the intent and fails after; any other commit fails as unattributed. Commits before that base are out of scope here (the old history check and, later, the legacy rule judge them). Expose it as a command (for example athena check --attribution) and add a non-blocking CI job on pushes to main and on schedule, beside the existing full-history check, listing .github/workflows/ci.yml as a governance deliverable. Tests: a properly landed squash passes; an unrecorded commit fails naming it; a pending one passes within 15 minutes and fails after; a records-branch commit that is not a fast-forward is reported.
